newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies approve shareholders rights bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies approve shareholders rights bill.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies approved a bill aimed at giving more power to minority shareholders, a congressional official said.
The bill, known as the Lei das SA, or the Company Law, was approved by a show of hands in the lower house and now advances to the Senate.

The law would give minority shareholders representing a minimum of five percent of a company's voting capital the right to demand confidential information and call a general assembly, the official said.
The official said the bill would smooth the way for privatization of Brazilian companies by setting down clear rules for minority shareholders' rights during mergers and cisions.

Several upcoming privatizations, like those of Telebras and Eletrobras, involve the separation of subsidiaries from holdings prior to their sale. Some minority shareholders believe they may lose out in the splits.
A report by the National Industry Confederation (CNI) said the bill would prevent the conversion of one type of share into another and increase investor interest in voting shares.
